name: Backfire
tagline: T-Mobile customers hand a scam call to an AI decoy that stops the payout and blocks the scammer
problem_context: reported lost to fraud by Americans in 2025, up from $12.5B in 2024
how_title: One tap turns a scam call into evidence that stops his payout

steps.label: Network sends only the caller's audio
Nemotron hears the scam: two beeps
Decoy gets the payout; agent checks it

real_vs_simulated: Real: a live phone call, Nemotron agents, domain and blockchain lookups, writes to Capital One's Nessie sandbox. Simulated: T-Mobile network, bank data, network blocks.
proof_title: Nemotron on a laptop caught 33 of 33 test scams

columns:
Local Nemotron Nano 4B
(runs the live demo)
rows: Tricks aimed at the AI caught

proof_models_note: Local Nemotron Nano 4B on a laptop GPU scores the live call; NVIDIA-hosted Nemotron is the fallback (never scored on our test set). On real phone calls the alert fired 12 to 18 s in.
metric_context: test scams caught, with 2 of 27 look-alike legit calls wrongly flagged
metric_method: 60 team-written synthetic scripts (33 scam, 27 legit), tuned on a separate dev set. Small sample. Test set re-scored after later fixes; a separate held-out set of 40 gave 20 of 20 and 1 of 20 false alarms.
tmobile_line: Protects before the ring, during the call and after; only the caller is ever analyzed.
nvidia_line: Nemotron detects, plays the decoy, then an agent plans lookups and proposes blocks.
capitalone_line: The payout account the decoy captures stops the customer's transfer and flags the mule account.
next_line: Pilot on T-Mobile's call servers, with a Capital One payee-risk feed.

story.persona_line: A customer picks up. Caller ID shows their bank.
story.persona_note: Synthetic scenario. Data: FTC Data Spotlight, Aug 2025 (ages 60+).
story.caller_quote: “Your account's being drained. Move your savings to a safe account. Don't tell anyone.”
story.stakes_title: Scams that start with a phone call cost the most
story.stakes_a_label: median loss when the scam starts with a phone call
story.stakes_b_label: median loss when it starts on social media
story.stakes_source: Reported losses, people 60+. Source: FTC, Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026, Oct 2026
story.gap_title: Once a scam call gets through, nothing helps them

gap_cols.head: Before the ring
gap_cols.body: Scam ID and Scam Block judge the number

gap_cols.head: After the call
gap_cols.body: They report it and never hear what happened

story.gap_source: Callback Protection warns only on outbound calls. Source: T-Mobile, Advancing Cybersecurity at T-Mobile, Nov 2026
story.flip_line: Not the caller picking up. The caller who dialed.
story.flip_caption: One tap hands the scammer to an AI that talks in their voice.
story.flip_privacy: Only the caller's side of the call is ever analyzed.

flip_proof.label: calls TPG Telecom diverted to AI “victims”: 100+ days of scammer time wasted
calls where scammers spotted the AI as a bot (about 5%, two studies)

story.flip_sources: Sources: GSMA case study, Apate.ai and TPG Telecom (Australia), Oct 2025 (longest call: 54 min). Bot recognition: Traister et al., arXiv 2609.29528, 2026 (10,015 calls); Sahin et al., USENIX SOUPS 2017 (200 calls).
story.loop_title: Follow the money, not the number
loop_rows: Capital One stops the customer's transfer and flags the account for every customer
T-Mobile Callback Protection warns anyone who dials it
Safe Web Browsing blocks it after one analyst click
story.loop_source: Capital One Nessie sandbox, mock data. T-Mobile actions simulated. Callback Protection: 67M+ warnings (Nov 2026).

persona_stat.label: as many older adults reported losing $10,000+ to fake bank, company or government impostors in 2024 as in 2020 (8,269 vs 1,790)
